name.title: Cornell Computational Game Society (Cornell CGS)
name.heading: Cornell Computational Game Society
name.description: We are training a Guandan AI. We built a poker equity calculator. We make our own mini games. Our bots learn by playing themselves. We have fun at our meetings. Flip the card and deal yourself in.

planes.title: Our members · Cornell CGS
planes.heading: Our members
planes.description: Elsie Lu (President), Evan Jiang (Recruitment Chair), Yicheng, Michael, Henrique, Eric, Selina, Christina, Daniel.

slope.title: The Slope to the sky · Cornell CGS
slope.heading: One table, a lot of hometowns
slope.description: Our members grew up all over this globe, and every hometown has its own card game. Teach us yours.

work.title: Five things we do · Cornell CGS
work.heading: Our royal flush
work.description: Guandan AI. Four bots play Guandan against each other and learn from every hand. Poker odds. Our hold’em calculator deals 20,000 hands to find your odds. Try it below.

stars.title: More deals than stars · Cornell CGS
stars.heading: More deals than stars
stars.description: Two decks. Four players. Guandan has more than 10⁴⁵ possible deals. The observable universe has about 10²² to 10²⁴ stars.

who.title: Who we are · Cornell CGS
who.heading: We build game AI, block by block.
who.description: We’re a student club at Cornell. Like the blocks in our logo, every project snaps onto the last one. We’ve made mini games and a poker calculator, and now we’re training a Guandan AI.

guandan.title: The Guandan AI · Cornell CGS
guandan.heading: Guandan AI
guandan.description: Four bots play the card game Guandan against each other and learn from every hand. No results published yet.

poker.title: The poker odds calculator · Cornell CGS
poker.heading: Poker odds
poker.description: Our hold’em calculator deals 20,000 hands to find your odds. Try it below.

code.title: Read the code · Cornell CGS
code.heading: Read the code
code.description: A Monte Carlo equity calculator for Texas hold’em. You can run it on our home page.

selfplay.title: How our AI learns · Cornell CGS
selfplay.heading: Self-play
selfplay.description: Frame. Turn the rules of the game into code. Simulate. Build a fast table where bots can play each other. Train. Let them play game after game and learn from every win and loss.

alphago.title: The AlphaGo story · Cornell CGS
alphago.heading: Watch the stones land.
alphago.description: DeepMind’s AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol in 2016, and it got that strong partly by playing against itself. We train our card game AIs the same way.

next.title: What comes next · Cornell CGS
next.heading: Next
next.description: Finish training our Guandan AI. Build an AI that solves Ink Maze. Let anyone play against our bots.
